title: visual-onboarding-artifact-standardization-and-localization-guardrails
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Release documentation, quickstart flows, and in-product onboarding use a mix of handcrafted screenshots and ad-hoc exports which are inconsistent in framing, naming, redaction, and localization readiness. This causes brand drift, slows release QA, and increases privacy risk when PII remains visible.

Goal: Define and implement a repeatable pipeline for onboarding and docs visuals that ensures brand-consistent framing, automated redaction, localization-safe cropping, and downstream metadata for asset selection and QA. The pipeline should produce artifacts that can be consumed by docs, marketing, and the onboarding engine with minimal manual edits.

Scope: v1 focuses on desktop web UIs and Console flows (primary hero screens for quickstarts and release notes). We will cover: export conventions, auto-crop heuristics, PII redaction masks, localization-safe crops (handle longer strings and RTL), color mode variants (light/dark), and a small human review step for edge cases.
requirements: Define canonical framing guidelines for 3 common onboarding screens: sign-up, model selection, and API key flow (margins, focal areas, and token/field display rules)
Implement an automated export script (Figma plugin + lightweight node tool) that exports assets at 1x/2x, applies recommended crop, and stamps metadata (locale, flow, model, git sha)
Integrate PII detection + redaction: run OCR + regex + heuristic PII detector, apply selectable masks (solid, blurred), and produce an audit log for reviewer
Design localization-safe crop rules that expand padding for locales with expected UI text expansion and support RTL mirroring for key flows
Produce style tokens and an asset checklist for marketing/docs teams (file naming, alt text, and canonical screenshot captions)
Add a small web UI for human-in-the-loop review where reviewers can approve, nudge crop, or escalate to engineering
Create a QA runbook and acceptance dashboard metrics (auto-redact accuracy, human override rate, time-to-approve)
Ship initial dataset: 60 canonical screenshots across 6 locales (en-US, fr-FR, de-DE, es-ES, ja-JP, ar-SA) with dark/light variants
acceptance_criteria: Automated pipeline exports assets that match the framing guide >= 90% of the time in CI runs
Auto-redaction reduces PII exposure to zero in the sample dataset (human QA confirmation)
Localization-safe crops avoid truncation for locales in the sample dataset and preserve focal elements
Assets include metadata (locale, screen-key, git-sha, export-timestamp) embedded in filename and sidecar JSON
Design and marketing teams have a documented checklist and a Figma + Drive folder with the canonical assets
Human-in-the-loop UI is available and reviewers can process the initial 60 assets within the planned 2-week QA window

2026-03-14 - Marisol Gomez: Implemented initial Figma plugin flow prototype and uploaded example exports to Drive. Filed GH PR with export script; link in attachments. Need backend support for storing sidecar JSONs (ENG dependency).
updates: 2026-03-11 - Decision: Use a dual-mode redaction approach. For textual PII (emails, tokens) default to solid masked boxes; for contextual personal data (usernames, identifiers) use a blur option to preserve layout context. Rationale: solid masks are safe for public docs; blur helps internal UX previews. Trade-off documented in PRD.

2026-03-12 - Trade-off: Automatic cropping will prefer top-left rule for hero cards to maintain brand logo visibility. This may cut off bottom-of-card callouts; added a 'preserve-focal' flag to allow manual override.
2026-03-13 - Blocker: Eng needed to provide endpoint for storing sidecar metadata. Raised dependency ENG-30821 (backend-metadata-store).

2026-03-14 - Progress: Figma plugin v0.1 exports 1x/2x assets and produces filenames matching the convention: <screen>-<locale>-<model>-<sha>-<ts>.png. Added a short video walkthrough in Drive for the marketing team.
2026-03-14 - Next steps: Hook up OCR/PII detector to the export pipeline, run the first sample batch (60 assets), and schedule human QA slot for 2026-03-17 to 2026-03-20.
notes: Keep export script idempotent — re-running should not overwrite approved assets unless explicitly forced.
Add a light-weight machine-readable sidecar (JSON) per asset with fields: screen_key, locale, dark_mode, focal_box, redaction_flags, exporter_version.
For initial v1, prefer manual review for any asset where OCR confidence < 0.85 or redaction detector confidence < 0.9.
Plan v2 to add automated cropping heuristics driven by rendered DOM selector snapshots (requires a lightweight headless-render service).
